key_insight: The paper combines Bayesian optimization and discrete biorthogonal wavelet analysis to rapidly find and robustly identify a laser frequency reference for auto-locking.
engineering_relevance: This improves practical laser stabilization for field-deployable quantum communication, quantum computing, and precision measurement systems.
method: Use Bayesian optimization to search the reference frequency efficiently from prior observations.
Apply discrete biorthogonal wavelet transformation to detect transition signals and identify the correct reference via invariant frequency spacing and relative amplitudes.
Lock the laser with a lead zirconate titanate-current double-servo loop to tighten the linewidth.
evidence_signal: The approach reportedly speeds up reference searching by 5× and achieves over 99.5% identification accuracy under strong disturbances, while narrowing the linewidth to 20 kHz.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate signal features and servo tuning, so real-world drift, noise, or hardware miscalibration may affect robustness.
paper_title: Rapid and robust laser-frequency auto-locking using Bayesian-optimization and discrete-wavelet-transformation algorithms
